title: Psalms Chapter 123 Quiz - Multi-Level
description: An enhanced quiz on Psalms chapter 123 with Easy, Medium, Hard, and Theological levels. Each level has 15 carefully crafted questions. Choose your difficulty and dive in!

easy.title: Psalms Chapter 123 Quiz - Easy Level
easy.description: Perfect for beginners! Test your basic knowledge of Psalms Chapter 123.

questions.question: In Psalms 123, which of the following appears FIRST in the chapter?
options: Unto thee lift I up mine eyes
Our eyes wait upon the LORD our God
As the eyes of servants look unto the hand of their masters
Behold, as the eyes of a maiden unto the hand of her mistress
questions.correctAnswer: Unto thee lift I up mine eyes
questions.explanation: The phrase 'Unto thee lift I up mine eyes' appears first in Psalms 123:1, which is the opening verse of the chapter.

questions.question: To whom does the psalmist lift up his eyes in Psalms 123:1?
options: O thou that dwellest in the heavens
questions.correctAnswer: O thou that dwellest in the heavens
questions.explanation: Psalms 123:1 states 'Unto thee lift I up mine eyes, O thou that dwellest in the heavens.'

questions.question: What type of song is Psalms 123 described as?
questions.explanation: Psalms 123:1 begins with 'A Song of degrees,' describing the type of song.

questions.question: According to Psalms 123:2, the eyes of servants look unto what?
questions.explanation: Psalms 123:2 says, 'as the eyes of servants look unto the hand of their masters.'

questions.question: In Psalms 123:2, the eyes of a maiden look unto what?
questions.explanation: Psalms 123:2 states, 'as the eyes of a maiden unto the hand of her mistress.'

questions.question: What do 'our eyes' wait upon according to Psalms 123:2?
questions.explanation: Psalms 123:2 says 'so our eyes wait upon the LORD our God.'

questions.question: Until when do our eyes wait upon the LORD our God in Psalms 123:2?
options: Until that he have mercy upon us
questions.correctAnswer: Until that he have mercy upon us
questions.explanation: Psalms 123:2 ends with 'until that he have mercy upon us.'

questions.question: Where does the one addressed in Psalms 123:1 dwell?
questions.explanation: Psalms 123:1 states 'O thou that dwellest in the heavens.'

questions.question: Which of these comparisons is made in Psalms 123:2?
options: Eyes of servants to the hand of their masters
Hands of servants to the feet of their masters
Feet of a maiden to the face of her mistress
Voices of servants to the words of their masters
questions.correctAnswer: Eyes of servants to the hand of their masters
questions.explanation: Psalms 123:2 compares 'the eyes of servants look unto the hand of their masters.'

questions.question: What is the attitude of 'our eyes' toward the LORD according to Psalms 123:2?
questions.explanation: Psalms 123:2 says 'so our eyes wait upon the LORD our God.'

questions.question: The psalmist lifts his eyes unto the one who dwells in which place?
questions.explanation: Psalms 123:1 states 'O thou that dwellest in the heavens.'

questions.question: True or False: Psalms 123 calls itself a Song of degrees.
questions.explanation: Psalms 123:1 opens with 'A Song of degrees,' confirming that it is called this.

questions.question: True or False: In Psalms 123, the eyes of servants look unto the hand of their masters.
questions.explanation: Psalms 123:2 states 'as the eyes of servants look unto the hand of their masters.'

questions.question: True or False: Psalms 123 says our eyes wait upon the hand of the mistress.
questions.explanation: Psalms 123:2 states our eyes wait upon the LORD our God, not upon the hand of the mistress.

questions.question: True or False: Psalms 123 mentions lifting hands in prayer.
questions.explanation: Psalms 123 does not mention lifting hands in prayer; it only mentions lifting eyes.

medium.title: Psalms Chapter 123 Quiz - Medium Level
medium.description: Ready for more? Apply biblical truths from Psalms Chapter 123 to real-life situations.

questions.question: What do the psalmists ask for in Psalms 123:3?
questions.explanation: The psalmists ask for mercy upon them, indicating their need for compassion from the Lord due to their situation, as stated in Psalms 123:3.

questions.question: What does Psalms 123:2 promise will happen if someone looks to the hand of the Lord?
options: They will be filled with contempt
questions.explanation: The verse indicates that as one waits upon the Lord, they do so with the expectation of receiving mercy, linking it to the plea in Psalms 123:3.

questions.question: What is the emotional state described in Psalms 123:3?
questions.explanation: The psalmist expresses that they are exceedingly filled with contempt, indicating a strong emotional response to their situation, as noted in Psalms 123:3.

questions.question: What do Psalms 123:1 and 123:2 together emphasize about the psalmist's attitude toward God?
questions.explanation: The psalmist lifts their eyes to the Lord and waits upon Him, showing a submissive and expectant attitude for mercy, as seen in both Psalms 123:1 and 123:2.

questions.question: What does the phrase 'exceedingly filled with the scorning of those that are at ease' imply in Psalms 123:4?
questions.explanation: This phrase illustrates the burden the psalmist feels from those who are comfortable and scornful, highlighting their difficult circumstances in Psalms 123:4.

questions.question: In Psalms 123:4, who is associated with contempt?
questions.explanation: The verse specifically mentions that the contempt is from the proud, indicating the source of the scorn that the psalmist feels, as stated in Psalms 123:4.

questions.question: What does the psalmist's lifting of eyes symbolize in Psalms 123:1?
questions.explanation: Lifting eyes to the Lord symbolizes a recognition of their need for help and mercy, embodying hope and dependence on God, as noted in Psalms 123:1.

questions.question: According to Psalms 123:2, how do the psalmists wait for the Lord?
questions.explanation: The psalmists wait with their eyes on the Lord, indicating an expectant attitude for His mercy, as expressed in Psalms 123:2.

questions.question: What kind of mercy are the psalmists seeking in Psalms 123:3?
questions.explanation: The repeated plea for mercy emphasizes their deep need for abundant mercy from the Lord in their distress, as stated in Psalms 123:3.

questions.question: What does the psalmist mean by 'scorning of those that are at ease' in Psalms 123:4?
questions.explanation: This phrase indicates that those at ease are scornful and dismissive of the psalmist's plight, contributing to their feelings of contempt, as noted in Psalms 123:4.

questions.question: The psalmist's plea for mercy indicates what about their situation?
options: They are in a position of strength
They are overwhelmed and in need
questions.correctAnswer: They are overwhelmed and in need
questions.explanation: The repeated call for mercy suggests the psalmist feels overwhelmed by their circumstances and recognizes their need for divine help, as seen in Psalms 123:3.

questions.question: The attitude of waiting upon the Lord in Psalms 123:2 is crucial for what type of prayer?
questions.explanation: Waiting upon the Lord suggests a posture of seeking and asking for mercy, characteristic of petitionary prayer, as indicated in Psalms 123:2.

questions.question: True or False: Psalms 123:4 describes feelings of contentment among the psalmists.
questions.explanation: Psalms 123:4 expresses feelings of scorn and contempt, indicating a lack of contentment.

questions.question: True or False: The psalmist expresses confidence in their own strength in Psalms 123:3.
questions.explanation: The psalmist is asking for mercy, showing reliance on God rather than confidence in their own strength, as stated in Psalms 123:3.

questions.question: True or False: Psalms 123:2 encourages believers to look solely to their own abilities.
questions.explanation: Psalms 123:2 encourages looking to the Lord, emphasizing dependence on Him rather than solely on personal abilities.

hard.title: Psalms Chapter 123 Quiz - Hard Level
hard.description: Challenge yourself with deep analysis and cross-biblical connections from Psalms Chapter 123.

questions.question: In Psalms 123:2, the psalmist compares the eyes of the servants and a maiden to what?
options: The eyes of servants look unto the hand of their masters
The eyes of servants are closed in prayer
The eyes of maidens reflect the stars
The eyes of children look to their parents
questions.correctAnswer: The eyes of servants look unto the hand of their masters
questions.explanation: Psalms 123:2 states, 'Behold, as the eyes of servants look unto the hand of their masters, and as the eyes of a maiden unto the hand of her mistress; so our eyes wait upon the LORD our God.'

questions.question: According to Psalms 123:2, why do the eyes of the psalmist wait upon the LORD?
options: Until that he have mercy upon us
questions.correctAnswer: Until that he have mercy upon us
questions.explanation: Psalms 123:2 ends with 'so our eyes wait upon the LORD our God, until that he have mercy upon us.'

questions.question: What phrase is repeated in Psalms 123:3 to emphasize the plea for divine compassion?
options: Have mercy upon us, O LORD, have mercy upon us
Deliver us from evil, O LORD
Bless us and keep us, O LORD
questions.correctAnswer: Have mercy upon us, O LORD, have mercy upon us
questions.explanation: Psalms 123:3 repeats the plea 'Have mercy upon us, O LORD, have mercy upon us,' emphasizing the earnest request for mercy.

questions.question: In Psalms 123:3, what reason is given for asking the LORD's mercy?
options: For we are exceedingly filled with contempt
questions.correctAnswer: For we are exceedingly filled with contempt
questions.explanation: Psalms 123:3 states, 'for we are exceedingly filled with contempt,' which is the reason given for the plea for mercy.

questions.question: What two groups are mentioned in Psalms 123:4 as sources of scorn and contempt?
options: Those that are at ease and the proud
questions.correctAnswer: Those that are at ease and the proud
questions.explanation: Psalms 123:4 states, 'Our soul is exceedingly filled with the scorning of those that are at ease, and with the contempt of the proud.'

questions.question: In Psalms 123:4, the term 'at ease' most likely refers to which cultural or social group?
options: Those who are complacent and self-satisfied
questions.correctAnswer: Those who are complacent and self-satisfied
questions.explanation: The phrase 'those that are at ease' in Psalms 123:4 refers to people who live comfortably and complacently, often ignoring the plight of others.

questions.question: What does the Hebrew word 'חָנֵּן' (chanen) in Psalms 123:2 mean?
questions.explanation: The Hebrew word 'חָנֵּן' (chanen) commonly means 'to show favor or mercy,' which aligns with the plea in Psalms 123:2 for God’s mercy.

questions.question: Which literary device is predominantly used in Psalms 123:2 when comparing the psalmist’s eyes to those of servants and a maiden?
questions.explanation: Psalms 123:2 uses 'as' to compare the eyes of servants and a maiden to the psalmist's eyes, which is a simile.

questions.question: Which New Testament passage echoes the theme of looking to God for mercy as expressed in Psalms 123:2?
options: Luke 18:13 - The tax collector’s plea for mercy
Revelation 21:4 - God wiping away all tears
John 3:16 - God’s love for the world
questions.correctAnswer: Luke 18:13 - The tax collector’s plea for mercy
questions.explanation: Luke 18:13 echoes the theme of seeking God's mercy as in Psalms 123:2, where the tax collector prays, 'God, be merciful to me, a sinner!'

questions.question: Which Old Testament passage is closely connected to the theme of humility and seeking God's mercy found in Psalms 123:3?
options: Isaiah 66:2 - God’s favor on the humble and contrite
Genesis 1:1 - Creation of the heavens and earth
questions.correctAnswer: Isaiah 66:2 - God’s favor on the humble and contrite
questions.explanation: Isaiah 66:2 states God looks favorably on the humble and contrite, which parallels the plea for mercy in Psalms 123:3.

questions.question: What comes immediately before the plea for mercy in Psalms 123:3?
options: The eyes waiting on the LORD
The lifting up of eyes to heaven
The mention of servants and maidens
questions.correctAnswer: The eyes waiting on the LORD
questions.explanation: Psalms 123:2 describes the eyes waiting on the LORD, which immediately precedes the plea for mercy in Psalms 123:3.

questions.question: What literary technique does Psalms 123:4 demonstrate by pairing 'scorning' with 'contempt' to describe the psalmist’s suffering?
questions.explanation: Psalms 123:4 uses synonymous parallelism by pairing similar ideas—'scorning' and 'contempt'—to emphasize the insult experienced.

questions.question: How does Psalms 123 reflect the cultural practice of raising eyes in expectation or supplication in the ancient Near East?
options: It uses the imagery of servants and maidens looking to their masters, symbolizing dependence
It recounts laws for temple worship
questions.correctAnswer: It uses the imagery of servants and maidens looking to their masters, symbolizing dependence
questions.explanation: Psalms 123:2 reflects the cultural practice by likening the psalmist’s gaze to that of servants and maidens looking expectantly to their masters for provision and favor.

questions.question: True or False: Psalms 123:4 mentions the 'scorning of those that are at ease' and the 'contempt of the proud'.
questions.explanation: Psalms 123:4 explicitly states 'Our soul is exceedingly filled with the scorning of those that are at ease, and with the contempt of the proud.'

questions.question: True or False: Psalms 123:1 describes the psalmist looking downwards to the earth for guidance.
questions.explanation: Psalms 123:1 states, 'Unto thee lift I up mine eyes, O thou that dwellest in the heavens,' indicating the psalmist looks upwards, not downwards.

theological.title: Psalms Chapter 123 Quiz - Theological Level
theological.description: Deep biblical theology from Psalms Chapter 123 that unites all believers. Explore foundational truths about God, creation, and humanity.

questions.question: What doctrine does Psalms 123:1 teach about God's nature?
questions.explanation: Psalms 123:1 shows that God is situated in the heavens, emphasizing His transcendence over creation.

questions.question: What doctrine does Psalms 123:2 teach about human sin?
questions.explanation: Psalms 123:2 illustrates the servant's reliance on their master, representing how humans should depend on God for mercy.

questions.question: What doctrine does Psalms 123:3 teach about salvation?
questions.explanation: Psalms 123:3 emphasizes the plea for mercy, highlighting that salvation is rooted in God's merciful nature.

questions.question: Which divine attribute does verse 1 specifically demonstrate?
questions.explanation: Verse 1 shows God dwelling in the heavens, illustrating His transcendence above earthly matters.

questions.question: Which divine attribute does verse 3 specifically demonstrate?
questions.explanation: Verse 3 is a direct plea for mercy from the LORD, showcasing His attribute of mercy.

questions.question: How does this chapter connect to, prepare for, or fulfill a theme elsewhere in Scripture?
options: The theme of lament in the Psalms
The call to worship in the New Testament
The promise of restoration in Isaiah
questions.correctAnswer: The theme of lament in the Psalms
questions.explanation: Psalms 123 reflects a lamenting tone, connecting to the broader theme of lament found throughout the Psalms.

questions.question: How does this chapter connect to the theme of mercy in the New Testament?
options: The concept of grace in Paul’s letters
The parable of the Good Samaritan
questions.explanation: The plea for mercy in Psalms 123 resonates with Jesus' teachings on mercy, as seen in the Sermon on the Mount.

questions.question: What combined doctrine do verses 2 and 4 teach about human suffering?
options: The role of pride in suffering
questions.explanation: Verses 2 and 4 together illustrate how believers are to respond to contempt and suffering with reliance on God.

questions.question: What combined doctrine do verses 1 and 3 teach about divine assistance?
questions.explanation: Verses 1 and 3 together express a plea for divine mercy, indicating that God is available to help those in need.

questions.question: What combined doctrine do verses 2 and 3 teach about the believer's posture before God?
questions.explanation: Verses 2 and 3 reflect a posture of desperate dependence on God while simultaneously holding hope for His mercy.

questions.question: Sceptics claim that the pleas for mercy in Psalms 123:3-4 indicate weakness. What does Psalms 123:3-4 actually teach?
questions.explanation: Psalms 123:3-4 highlights the strength in recognizing one's need for God's mercy amidst contempt and scorn.

questions.question: What doctrine does Psalms 123:4 teach about human pride?
questions.explanation: Psalms 123:4 points to the relationship between pride and contempt, indicating that pride results in scorn towards others.

questions.question: Which divine attribute does verse 4 specifically demonstrate?
questions.explanation: Verse 4 reflects God's longsuffering nature as He observes the scorn of the proud, enduring their contempt.

questions.question: What combined doctrine do verses 1 and 4 teach about the believer's experience?
questions.explanation: Verses 1 and 4 together highlight the believer's call to lift their eyes to God while enduring the scorn of the proud.

questions.question: How does Psalms 123 connect to the overall theme of dependence found in the Psalms?
options: It reflects individual dependence on God
questions.correctAnswer: It reflects individual dependence on God
questions.explanation: Psalms 123 embodies the theme of individual dependence on God, calling for His mercy and help.
